summary: Panel component for interactive on/off buttons, including momentary, toggle, radio, and exclusive button behavior. Use it as UI state and read it through Panel CHOP, callbacks, exports, or Python panel values.

key_params.name: buttontype
key_params.note: Momentary, toggle, radio, or exclusive button behavior.

key_params.name: buttongroup
key_params.note: Radio group label for buttons in the same component.

key_params.name: buttongroupdat
key_params.note: Table DAT listing button paths for a radio group across components.

key_params.name: scaletofit
key_params.note: Scale label text to fit the panel.

key_params.name: fontsize
key_params.note: Panel font size in resolution-independent units.

key_params.name: textpadding
key_params.note: Text padding from the panel edges.

key_params.name: x
key_params.note: Panel X position relative to parent.

key_params.name: y
key_params.note: Panel Y position relative to parent.

key_params.name: hmode
key_params.note: Horizontal size mode: fixed, fill, or anchors.

key_params.name: vmode
key_params.note: Vertical size mode: fixed, fill, or anchors.

key_params.name: alignallow
key_params.note: Whether this panel follows parent alignment.

key_params.name: clickthrough
key_params.note: Ignore mouse clicks on this panel.

key_params.name: opacity
key_params.note: Panel opacity from the Look page.

key_concepts: click(val, clickCount, force, left, middle, right)
common_gotchas: Button Type is the official behavior control; use momentary, toggle, radio, or exclusive modes instead of inventing a generic toggle parameter.
Button Group Label only groups buttons located in the same component, so scattered radio groups need Button Group DAT instead.
Button Group DAT can list scattered button paths and supports Pattern Matching, but activating a listed button modifies the radio panel values of the DAT parent.
A Button COMP is UI state, not a CHOP by itself; use Panel CHOP, callbacks, exports, or Python panel values to drive a network.
Changing Display can trigger layout work; use opacity for lightweight visual hiding when interaction/layout should remain stable.
